The checkpoint\n * read is a DYNAMIC import: this module's STATIC chain must not grow (suites\n * that partial-mock `@papercusp/flags/server` — send.test — import it; a new\n * static store chain here re-arms the flags/server partial-mock trap). The\n * tail is decoration on decoration: any failure just omits it. The combined\n * snippet stays within `budget.snippetChars` (the tail eats into the title's\n * share, never past the cap).\n */\nexport const bodyRefWorkItemResolver: RefResolver = async (ref, budget) => {\n  if (ref.kind !== 'work-item') return null;\n  // WI-NNN ids are allocated from a per-database sequence and can repeat in\n  // different harnesses. A free-prose mention with no stamped harness has no\n  // safe target; keep the author's id visible and omit the optional decoration.\n  if (!ref.harness && /^WI-\\d+$/i.test(ref.id)) return null;\n  const wi = await getWorkItem(ref.id, ref.harness);\n  if (!wi || (ref.harness && wi.harness !== ref.harness)) return null;\n  const assignee = wi.assignee ? ` @${shortHandle(wi.assignee)}` : '';\n  const terminalSubject = terminalSubjectFor(wi);\n  const scope = ref.harness ? ` in ${ref.harness}` : '';\n  const label = wi.id + ' [' + wi.kind + '/' + workItemDisplayState(wi) + scope + assignee + ']';\n  let tail = '';\n  try {\n    const [{ getWorkItemCheckpoint }, { activeWorkspaceId }] = await Promise.all([\n      import('../../work-item-checkpoint'),\n      import('../../workspace-registry'),\n    ]);\n    const cp = await getWorkItemCheckpoint({\n      workItemId: wi.id,\n      harness: wi.harness,\n      workspaceId: activeWorkspaceId(),\n    });\n    if (cp) tail = ` ⌁ ${clampSnippetTail(cp, BODY_REF_CHECKPOINT_TAIL_CHARS)}`;\n  } catch {\n    /* fail-soft: no tail */\n  }\n  const head = workItemSnippet(wi, Math.max(0, budget.snippetChars - tail.length));\n  return {\n    label,\n    snippet: `${head}${tail}`,\n    ...(terminalSubject ? { terminalSubject } : {}),\n  };\n};\n\n/**\n * Plan-item body resolver factory (coordination/ref-hydrate.ts consumer:\n * coord:dispatch / coord:handoff, WI-4165 — \"hydrate assigned plan-item\n * bodies into coord:dispatch / handoff deliveries\"): resolves a\n * `{kind:'plan-item', slug, item}` ref into that item's own text +\n * effectiveStatus off the PG-canonical plan row (the SAME resolution\n * plans:get-item / plans:items / plans:set-status agree on — EI-356).\n *\n * NOT part of DEFAULT_RESOLVERS: unlike msg/work-item (global stores), a plan\n * item's harness scope varies per call site (a dispatch/handoff's own\n * `harness` arg, defaulting to the plan's own harness when omitted) — each\n * consumer binds its own resolver via this factory and installs it through\n * `resolvers`, the same injection contract P-006 (gate) and P-004\n * (owner-turn) already use for consumer-owned stores.\n */\nexport function makePlanItemResolver(harness?: string): RefResolver {\n  return async (ref, budget) => {\n    if (ref.kind !== 'plan-item') return null;\n    const row = await getPlanRow(ref.slug, harness ? { harnessSlug: harness } : {});\n    if (!row) return null;\n    const { items } = resolveEffectiveStatusForItems(planItemsForRow(row));\n    const item = items.find((i) => i.id === ref.item);\n    if (!item) return null;\n    return {\n      label: `plan:${ref.slug}#${ref.item} [${item.effectiveStatus}]`,\n      snippet: clampSnippet(item.text, budget.snippetChars),\n    };\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `refs` (budget-deduped, first-N) into render-ready hydrations, in\n * parallel, each fail-soft. Order of the returned list follows the budgeted\n * input order.\n */\n/**\n * P-006: resolve a sender's gateRefs (announced-gate event keys) into\n * send-time-verified stamps — checked against the announced-gates store the\n    // senders already set. This is the IO half (the renderer stays pure);\n    // best-effort BY CONTRACT — any failure ⇒ undefined map ⇒ plain lines.\n    // Acks are skipped (a pure receipt glyph — quoting what was acked is\n    // noise); a dangling ref still renders, marked unresolved (visible, not\n    // papered over). Capped to the shown-window size, newest-biased to match\n    // renderInjection's newest-kept overflow policy.\n    let relatedQuotes: Map<string, HydratedRef> | undefined;\n    try {\n      const relatedIds = [\n        ...new Set(\n          (injectionEntries as unknown as Array<Record<string, unknown>>)\n            .filter(\n              (en) =>\n                en.kind !== \"ack\" &&\n                typeof en.related_msg_id === \"string\" &&\n                en.related_msg_id,\n            )\n            .map((en) => en.related_msg_id as string),\n        ),\n      ].slice(-RELATED_QUOTE_MAX_REFS);\n      if (relatedIds.length) {\n        const hydrated = await measureInboxPhase(\"related-message-hydration\", () =>\n          hydrateRefs(\n            relatedIds.map((id) => ({ kind: \"msg\" as const, id })),\n            { budget: { snippetChars: RELATED_QUOTE_SNIPPET_CHARS, maxRefs: relatedIds.length } },\n          ),\n        );\n        relatedQuotes = new Map(\n          hydrated.flatMap((h) => (h.ref.kind === \"msg\" ? [[h.ref.id, h] as const] : [])),\n        );\n      }\n    } catch {\n      relatedQuotes = undefined;\n    }\n    // coord-authority-hardening P-008: auto-detect WI-/EI- ids loose in the\n    // shown FREE-PROSE lines and hydrate each distinct id ONCE into a one-line\n    // status + title + checkpoint-tail suffix at delivery — the receiver stops\n    // re-fetching or half-remembering cited items. Same IO-half contract as the\n    // P-005 block above: best-effort BY CONTRACT (any failure ⇒ undefined map ⇒\n    // plain lines). Machine-stamped lifecycle / plan-event / ack lines are\n    // excluded (their ids are structural, not citations — isBodyRefEligible),\n    // and a sender's noBodyRefs opt-out is honored here (no lookups) and again\n    // at render. A local miss stays SILENT — unlike a declared ref, an\n    // auto-detected mention carries no promise this store can resolve it (a\n    // federated peer's id, prose that merely looks like an id); the id still\n    // travels verbatim in the prose. Newest-biased global cap, like P-005.\n    let bodyRefs: Map<string, HydratedRef> | undefined;\n    try {\n      const refByKey = new Map<string, HydratableRef>();\n      for (const en of injectionEntries as unknown as Array<Record<string, unknown>>) {\n        if (!isBodyRefEligible(en) || readBodyRefsOptOut(en)) continue;\n        for (const ref of detectEntryBodyRefs(en)) {\n          if (ref.kind === \"work-item\") refByKey.set(canonicalRefKey(ref), ref);\n        }\n      }\n      const refs = [...refByKey.values()].slice(-BODY_REF_MAX_TOTAL);\n      if (refs.length) {\n        const hydrated = await measureInboxPhase(\"work-item-body-reference-hydration\", () =>\n          hydrateRefs(\n            refs,\n            {\n              budget: { snippetChars: BODY_REF_SNIPPET_CHARS, maxRefs: refs.length },\n              resolvers: { \"work-item\": bodyRefWorkItemResolver },\n            },\n          ),\n        );\n        bodyRefs = new Map(\n          hydrated.flatMap((h) =>\n            h.ref.kind === \"work-item\" ? [[canonicalRefKey(h.ref), h] as const] : [],\n          ),\n        );\n      }\n    } catch {\n      bodyRefs = undefined;\n    }\n    const coordInjection = renderInjection(\n      injectionEntries as unknown as CoordLineSource[],\n      { cueScope, relatedQuotes, bodyRefs },\n    );\n\n    // P-010 re-bootstrap-on-compaction (D-007): on the first read after a fresh\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":38453}},"started_at_ms":1791602928679,"completed_at_ms":1791602928679}}

[[h.ref.id, h] as const] : [])),\\n        );\\n      }\\n    } catch {\\n      relatedQuotes = undefined;\\n    }\\n    // coord-authority-hardening P-008: auto-detect WI-/EI- ids loose in the\\n    // shown FREE-PROSE lines and hydrate each distinct id ONCE into a one-line\\n    // status + title + checkpoint-tail suffix at delivery — the receiver stops\\n    // re-fetching or half-remembering cited items. [[canonicalRefKey(h.ref), h] as const] : [],\\n          ),\\n        );\\n      }\\n    } catch {\\n      bodyRefs = undefined;\\n    }\\n    const coordInjection = renderInjection(\\n      injectionEntries as unknown as CoordLineSource[],\\n      { cueScope, relatedQuotes, bodyRefs },\\n    );\\n\\n    // P-010 re-bootstrap-on-compaction (D-007): on the first read after a fresh\\n\"}"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a123c3-d240-7f43-a110-aa6a2c95b533","create_time":1791602930.3537796}},"metadata":{"client_authored":false,"fallback_token_limit_override":12000}}

harness?: string,\n  opts: WorkItemReadOptions = {},\n): Promise<WorkItem[]> {\n  if (ids.length === 0) return [];\n  const uniqueIds = [...new Set(ids)];\n  const issues = await issuesByIds(uniqueIds, opts);\n  const byId = new Map<string, WorkItem>(issues.map((issue) => [issue.id, issueToWorkItem(issue)]));\n  const featureIds = uniqueIds.filter((id) => !byId.has(id));\n  const features = await featuresByIds(featureIds, harness, opts);\n  for (const feature of features) byId.set(feature.id, feature);\n  return ids.flatMap((id) => {\n    const item = byId.get(id);\n    return item ? [item] : [];\n  });\n}\n\n/** The label this consumer's coverage verdict is reported under (WI-9393). */\nconst WORK_ITEM_SEARCH_COVERAGE_SOURCE = 'work_items:search';\n/**\n * The vector surfaces this search actually reads — ONE, despite two families.\n *\n * VERIFIED against the catalog rather than assumed: the feature-family source\n * selects from `harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated`, which is a VIEW\n * (`pg_class.relkind='v'`) defined as\n *   `SELECT …, embedding, embedding_mode, … FROM harness_shared.work_items\n *      WHERE item_kind <> ALL (ARRAY['bug','change','task'])`\n * — the SAME physical table and the SAME `embedding` column the issue-family\n * source reads. {"timestamp":"2026-10-10T03:31:57.646Z","ordinal":788,"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call_output","id":"ctco_01a123de-0e4e-72a1-906c-0981fef43f52","call_id":"call_7f422389eac64dee8a6cdb620b4147a1","output":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"{\"direct\":\"function\",\"tool\":\"mcp__papercusp_su__work_items_checkpoint\",\"description\":\"Get oriented ONCE per session-with-context (a user task you have\\nnot seen this run) — by whichever of these two routes your host gave you:\\n\\n  **ROLE-SCOPED OVERRIDE:** The routes below assume a role permitted to use coordination\\n  writes. The evidence-only judge role is intentionally excluded from coordination-write\\n  tools, so it must not call coord:declare-intent, claim plan lanes, or pass intent to\\n  coord:orient (that causes an internal declaration attempt). Judges may call coord:orient\\n  {} without intent for omitted read context, then work only the item already routed to\\n  them. This omits memory recall and intent declaration by design.\\n\\n  **ROUTE A — an `## Orientation` block already arrived in this turn.** Your held\\n  work-items, unanswered directed messages, and whether a wake source (armed loop)\\n  exists came WITH it: the server read them for you. Do NOT spend a\\n  `coord:orient` round-trip re-fetching them — you are oriented. Claim your lane\\n  with `coord:declare-intent { intent, items }`, and reach for\\n  `coord:orient` only for what that block deliberately EXCLUDES: the claimable\\n  backlog, full inbox bodies, a mem0 recall. Judge by PRESENCE ONLY — the block is\\n  emitted just when that state CHANGES, and only to hosts that inject it, so its\\n  ABSENCE never means \\\"you are oriented\\\".\\n\\n  **ROUTE B — no such block.** Bootstrap in ONE call:\\n  **`coord:orient { intent }`** — pass your one-line intent for the\\n  task. In a SINGLE round-trip it returns your current assignments\\n  (+ lane + load), the claimable backlog, your unread inbox summary,\\n  the recent plan-events delta, AND a mem0 recall for `intent` — and\\n  it DECLARES `intent` to peers so they see what you're working on.\\n  After a SUCCESSFUL orient, do NOT separately call `coord:plan-events`,\\n  `memory:search`, `coord:inbox`, or `coord:declare-intent` — orient's\\n  result ALREADY contains them (plan-events delta + inbox summary + a mem0\\n  recall) and ALREADY declared your intent; re-calling them just re-pays the\\n  round-trip orient collapsed. Reach for one individually only for a detail\\n  orient deliberately bounds (full inbox bodies, or a mem0 query OTHER than\\n  your intent).\\n\\n  - **Claim your lane.** When the work is plan items, pass them:\\n    `coord:orient { intent, planSlug, planItems: ['P-001', …] }` CLAIMS\\n    those items for you (and releases ones you've moved off). An unclaimed\\n    lane is invisible to the Mug and peers, so work gets double-placed.\\n    (Flipping an item `wip` via `plans:set-status` also auto-claims;\\n    `done` releases. A `claim_conflict` means a live peer holds it —\\n    coordinate with the holder, don't take it.)\\n  - **mem0 (what you know).** orient's recall uses `intent` as the query;\\n    pass `harness` for project-specific facts. Each mem0 hit carries an\\n    `id` — if the user later contradicts something, `memory:forget`\\n    that id. Use `memoryQuery` for a different query, or call\\n    `memory:search` directly. A recall hit is BINDING context, not flavor:\\n    if a recalled fact prescribes a behavior for THIS task, follow it — or\\n    explicitly say why you're not.\\n  - **insights (how things work).** When you hit a confusing failure,\\n    `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section before grepping code —\\n    many \\\"weird bugs\\\" already have a written runbook.\\n  - **State answers NOW; only the append-only log answers EVER.** `coord:presence` /\\n    `fleet:assignments` are LIVE-STATE — who is alive, who holds what RIGHT NOW; an ended\\n    agent loses its fleet_slug and its presence row is TTL-reaped, so they CANNOT answer an\\n    *ever / was / missed / history* question. Route those to `coord:catch-up { audience }`\\n    (as a member of the fleet/topic) or `coord:feed { audience }` (the firehose) instead —\\n    never a state tool. Full map:\\n    `docs:search` `agent-insights/presence-vs-history-who-is-on-what`.\\n\\nRight layer for READS and WRITES — the memory↔docs boundary:\\n  - **HOW IT WORKS** (a runbook, a failure mode, why-something-is, a hard-won gotcha):\\n    READ via `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section; WRITE a new/updated MDX under\\n    `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/` with a `documents:` frontmatter\\n    anchor to the code it describes. This is the RIGHT place — a doc is code-ANCHORED,\\n    drift-TRACKED (the freshness sweep) and AUTO-HEALED (the doc-steward); a mem0 vector cannot\\n    be anchored/swept/auto-rewritten, so how-it-works left only in mem0 silently rots. Do NOT\\n    park a runbook in mem0.\\n  - **WHY a subsystem/decision is the way it is** (the rationale behind a design, not how it works):\\n    READ via `rationale:feed { topic }` — a topic-keyed projection over the relevant\\n    plan-decisions + work-items + insights, kept fresh by the event engine (`topics:list` for the\\n    topic, then `plans:get`/`docs:get` on an entry's `ref` for the full text). The discoverable\\n    \\\"why\\\" layer — reach for it before grepping plans/decisions by hand.\\n  - **A durable PERSONAL/PREFERENCE fact** (who the user is, a convention, an owner pref):\\n    READ via `memory:search`; WRITE via `memory:remember`. Keep mem0 entries SHORT, and when\\n    the why already lives in a doc/plan store only the non-derivable fact + a POINTER\\n    (`[[<plan-slug>]]`, `/internal/docs/agent-insights/<slug>`), never a copied paragraph.\\n  - **In-flight state** → coord; **derivable session state** (X shipped, migration N, N tests)\\n    → the plan / work-item, never memory.\\nSee the plans `papercusp-su-memory-2026-05-25` and\\n`tool-call-batching-wrappers-2026-06-21`.\\n\\n## Your tool surface is DYNAMIC — the whole 959-tool catalog is reachable on demand\\n\\nYour loaded tool list is usually a small CORE set (the default). Any tool NOT in it is still\\nreachable — you do not need everything loaded up front:\\n- **`tools:find(\\\"<what you want to do>\\\")`** — intent search; matched tools are activated so you can call them directly next.\\n- **`tools:invoke({ name, args })`** — call ANY tool by exact name without loading it (the universal fallback).\\nWhen you need a capability that isn't in your loaded set, SEARCH for it — don't assume it doesn't exist.\\n⚠ Your CLIENT's own tool search (Claude Code ToolSearch, OMP search_tool_bm25) indexes ONLY this\\nadvertised subset — a zero-hit search THERE does NOT mean the tool doesn't exist (EI-9011: agents\\nhit this and degraded to polling). A newer recorded-live successor row\n    // wins (the query reads only the latest row per owner), and the psu-host\n    // positive rescue below still applies. Best-effort: a read failure degrades\n    // to the older verdict, never to a death claim. Deferred through a thunk so a\n    // throwing accessor (a partial test mock) lands in the catch, not the batch.\n    timeAsync('enrichment', 'endedRecordedOwnerIds', () =>\n      Promise.resolve().then(() => endedRecordedOwnerIds(localAllIds)))\n      .then((s) => {\n        recordedEndedOwners = s;\n      })\n      .catch(() => {}),\n    // On-desktop (live OS window) owners — best-effort, box-local (empty on a\n    // headless box). Independent of the other joins so a wmctrl hiccup never\n    // affects wakeability/tier-1, and vice-versa.\n    timeAsync('enrichment', 'gatherOnDesktopSessions', () =>\n      gatherOnDesktopSessions({\n        ...(targeted ? { ownerIds: localAllIds } : {}),\n        onDiagnostic: (diagnostic) => reportDiagnostic({\n          phase: 'enrichment',\n          name: `gatherOnDesktopSessions.${diagnostic.name}`,\n          elapsedMs: diagnostic.elapsedMs,\n          status: diagnostic.status,\n        }),\n      }))\n      .then((s) => {\n        onDesktopOwners = s.owners;\n      })\n      .catch(() => {}),\n    // PTY-panel viewer-attach owners (pty-viewer-heartbeat.ts) — the no-OS-window\n    // sibling of on-desktop. Best-effort + independent so a DB hiccup never affects\n    // the other joins.\n    timeAsync('enrichment', 'gatherViewerAttachedOwners', () => gatherViewerAttachedOwners())\n      .then((s) => {\n        viewerAttachedOwners = s;\n      })\n      .catch(() => {}),\n    // Named-fleet membership (P-005) — best-effort + independent of the other joins.\n    timeAsync('enrichment', 'fetchPresenceFleet', () => fetchPresenceFleet(localAllIds))\n      .then((m) => {\n  return [header, ...lines].join('\\n');\n}\n\n/**\n * P-010 re-bootstrap-on-compaction (D-007). If the agent's cursor carries a\n * pending re-bootstrap (its cached roster baseline was lost to a context\n * compaction / fresh resume while this durable cursor kept advancing), build the\n * snapshot block + clear the flag ONCE, so the agent re-establishes its baseline\n * before trusting deltas and is never re-injected on later turns. Returns the\n * block, or null when no re-bootstrap is pending. `build` runs BEFORE the clear,\n * so a transient build failure leaves the flag set to retry next turn.\n *\n * The caller passes the already-read watermark (it reads it concurrently with\n * the inbox), so this adds no extra read on the common (no-flag) path.\n */\nexport async function consumePresenceRebootstrap(\n  ownerId: string,\n  wm: Pick<Watermark, 'snapshot_rebootstrap_pending'>,\n  build: () => Promise<string>,\n): Promise<string | null> {\n  if (!wm.snapshot_rebootstrap_pending) return null;\n  const block = await build();\n  await writeWatermark(ownerId, { snapshot_rebootstrap_pending: false });\n  return block;\n}\n *  per sweep. The window list has its own TTL; this also caches the PG join. */\nconst ON_DESKTOP_TTL_MS = 5000;\nlet onDesktopCache: { at: number; sets: OnDesktopSets } | null = null;\n\n/** Injectable seams for gatherOnDesktopSessions so the ancestry pass unit-tests\n *  without a live psu-pty dir or /proc. Production defaults wire the real ones. */\nexport interface GatherOnDesktopDeps {\n  /** Open-window enumerator. Default: listOpenWindows() (wmctrl). */\n  listWindows?: () => Promise<OpenWindow[]>;\n  /** Live interactive psu hosts (ownerId + host pid). Default: listLiveHostsAsync() (WI-10004587). */\n  listHosts?: () => Array<{ ownerId: string; pid: number }> | Promise<Array<{ ownerId: string; pid: number }>>;\n  /** Targeted counterpart to listHosts. Default: findLiveHostAsync(ownerId). */\n  findHost?: (ownerId: string) => Promise<{ ownerId: string; pid: number } | null>;\n  /** Recent launch candidates. Same self-validation as findLiveHost (recorded ownerId\n * present, socket exists, pid alive, psu-host identity — WI-2339 defect #2) so a\n * crashed host's leftover file or a recycled pid is skipped. Consumers include\n * desktop-window-liveness's ancestry-based on-desktop detection (WI-1586) — the\n * live host pid is the one session handle that cannot rot. Best-effort: a missing\n * dir or unreadable file yields fewer hosts, never a throw.\n *\n * ASYNC ONLY, by design (WI-10004559, WI-10004587). The directory scan, the per-host\n * meta read and the socket check all touch the shared psu-pty directory (~3.5k\n * entries), which holds the calling thread in D-state (wchan iterate_dir) for 20s+\n * during an ext4 journal stall. The\n *  host renames its staging file within the same synchronous call that wrote it,\n *  so an hour is several orders of magnitude of margin. */\nexport const ABANDONED_TEMP_MAX_AGE_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;\n\n/** The host's atomic-write staging name: `<target>.<pid>.tmp` (psu-pty-host.mjs\n *  writeMeta and the events-ledger trim). */\nconst ATOMIC_STAGING_RE = /\\.\\d+\\.tmp$/;\n\n/** Unlink staging files in `entries` older than `maxAgeMs`. Reuses the caller's\n *  directory listing so the janitor iterates the directory once. Returns the count. */\nasync function pruneAbandonedTempFilesAsync(\n  dir: string,\n  entries: readonly string[],\n  nowMs: number,\n  maxAgeMs: number,\n): Promise<number> {\n  let removed = 0;\n  for (const f of entries) {\n    if (!ATOMIC_STAGING_RE.test(f)) continue;\n    const p = join(dir, f);\n    try {\n      const st = await fsp.stat(p);\n      if (!st.isFile() || nowMs - st.mtimeMs < maxAgeMs) continue;\n      await fsp.unlink(p);\n      removed += 1;\n    } catch {\n      /* raced with its writer or another sweep — skip */\n    }\n  }\n  return removed;\n}\n\n/**\n * Remove discovery files (+ their sockets) whose host is no longer a live psu session\n * (WI-2510). `pruneDead()` in psu-pty-host.mjs runs ONLY opportunistically — when a NEW\n * host boots on the box, scanning every file — so on a box with no new psu launches for\n * hours, a dead host's `~/.papercusp/psu-pty/<owner>.json` (+ orphaned socket) lingers\n * indefinitely (a slow disk leak; `listLiveHostsAsync` also pays a per-file /proc read as they\n * accumulate). WI-2339 fix B already closed the correctness risk (a stale file can no\n * longer masquerade as a live host, via `pidIsPsuHost`'s cmdline cross-check), so this is\n * pure hygiene — it reuses the EXACT SAME liveness test `findLiveHost`/`listLiveHostsAsync` apply\n25-  sendMessage,\n26-} from \"../messages\";\n27-import { heartbeatPresence, getPresence } from \"../presence\";\n28-import { createPresenceBeatThrottle } from \"../presence-beat-throttle\";\n29:import { readWatermark, writeWatermark } from \"../watermarks\";\n30-import { emptyWatermark } from \"@papercusp/coordination/core\";\n31-import {\n32-  resolvePresenceScope,\n33-  assemblePresenceSnapshot,\n34-  renderPresenceRebootstrapBlock,\n35:  consumePresenceRebootstrap,\n36-} from \"../presence-snapshot\";\n37-// The default-visibility predicates, relocated out of this defineTool module so\n38-// the unread counter can share them (P-005 / D-006 — see the re-export below).\n39-import {\n--\n1237-              : undefined,\n1238-          ),\n1239-      )),\n1240-      measureInboxPhase(\"read-watermark\", () =>\n1241:        readWatermark(identity.ownerId).catch(() => emptyWatermark()),\n1242-      ),\n1243-    ]);\n1244-    tracePresenceRebootstrap = wm.snapshot_rebootstrap_pending === true;\n1245-    // WI-10005678: a verified spawn session (an acceptance judge) reads as\n--\n1610-        workspaceId?: string | null;\n1611-        harnessSlug?: string | null;\n1612-      };\n1613-      rebootstrap = await measureInboxPhase(\"consume-presence-rebootstrap\", () =>\n1614:        consumePresenceRebootstrap(\n1615-          identity.ownerId,\n1616-          wm,\n1617-          async () => {\n1618-            const resolved = await measureInboxPhase(\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":48904}},"started_at_ms":1791603181815,"completed_at_ms":1791603181815}}
